Research/2025-26/Early universe

Early universe

Primordial Black Hole Formation from QCD-like Equation-of-State Transitions

A numerical-relativity study of how an early-universe phase transition can change the threshold for black-hole collapse.

Research question

What did the project ask?

How do the depth and duration of a QCD-like softening of the early universe's equation of state affect the threshold for primordial-black-hole collapse?

Significance

Why does it matter?

Primordial-black-hole production is highly sensitive to the collapse threshold, and QCD-era formation naturally corresponds to roughly solar-mass black holes.

Method

What did the team do?

The team evolved spherical overdensities with a one-dimensional Misner-Sharp relativistic-collapse solver, distinguished the equation-of-state parameter from the sound speed, and tested parametric crossover widths and depths after benchmarking the solver in radiation domination.

Principal result

What did the evidence show?

The solver reproduced the radiation-era threshold within 1.3%. In the chosen QCD-like model, broadening the transition lowered the collapse threshold by approximately 27-44%, showing a large but strongly model-dependent sensitivity in the predicted abundance.
